source: Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — booklet 'ដំណាំពោត' (Corn Crop), Issue 1, 2003, funded by Asian Development Bank (ADB), Loan/Grant No. 1445-CAM(SF), sections on crop care, thinning, and weeding/hilling
text:
Care after planting: 2-3 days after sowing, farmers should check the germination rate. If germination is below 90%, gap-filling/reseeding may need to be considered, though this is not always strictly necessary — attention should be paid to seeding quality and seeding rate overall to help ensure good yield.

Thinning: about 15 days after germination, or once plants have 3-4 leaves and reach a height of 10-15cm, thin the seedlings so that only 1-2 plants remain at each planting point/hill, according to the row and hill spacing used.

Weeding and hilling (earthing up): after thinning out weak seedlings, weeding begins using a hoe. A second round of weeding takes place at around 40 days of corn age, or from when the plant has 6-8 leaves through the flowering stage; this second round is typically combined with hilling soil up around the base of the plant using a hoe, which helps new roots emerge and prevents stunted growth. Corn roots can extend about 3-4 rows within the furrow/row spacing and 1-2 rows along the planting row. Hilling up soil is understood to improve yield by reducing lodging, since the corn root system is fibrous and relatively shallow.
